question.text: How many risk levels does the Risk-o-meter show?

explanation.text: The Logic: Under SEBI's mutual-fund Risk-o-meter framework, schemes are classified into six bands: Low, Low to Moderate, Moderate, Moderately High, High, and Very High. The six-level scale is the standard industry depiction shown on scheme documents and monthly disclosures so investors can quickly compare relative scheme risk. The Trap: Three- or five-level scales are common simplifications but do not match the current SEBI Risk-o-meter format. The exact count is six because the regulator added intermediate bands ("Low to Moderate" and "Moderately High") to give finer differentiation. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B (MFF) workbook supports the existence and disclosure purpose of the Risk-o-meter, but the pages checked did not explicitly list the six categories or state the count "6". The six-level structure above is general SEBI/industry knowledge regarding the current Risk-o-meter framework.
